html:
The oldest known chariots with spoked wheels come from graves of the Sintashta culture in the southern Ural steppe, on today's border of Russia and Kazakhstan. They date to around 2000 BCE.

At sites such as Sintashta and Krivoye Ozero, warriors were buried with light two wheeled carts, the horses that pulled them, and weapons. Only the stains of the wooden wheels survive in the soil, but the spokes can still be counted. Spoked wheels were far lighter than the solid wheels of earlier wagons, so a pair of horses could pull the cart at speed.

The chariot spread fast across Eurasia and changed war for a thousand years.

  • In the Near East, the Hittites and Egyptians fought the great chariot battle of Kadesh around 1274 BCE.
  • The Hyksos are often credited with bringing it to Egypt.
  • In India the Rigveda is full of chariots.
  • In China, the Shang buried chariots by about 1200 BCE.

Many scholars link the Sintashta people to the early speakers of Indo Iranian languages.
